note: Hand-picked. Each summary is written in our own words from the linked article; add, edit or remove entries here. group: "background" puts an entry under Background reading.

items.title: AT&T says close to 500 AI agent workflows are now live
items.summary: A weekly roundup leads with AT&T: the carrier reports nearly 500 agent-run workflows in day-to-day operations, more than a million transactions a month, and a plan to triple that count within a year. The point for adoption teams is that whole processes were redesigned, not just given a chatbot.

items.title: Services firms are packaging 'get out of pilot' help for mid-size companies
items.summary: This week's worktech roundup includes Syntax opening a Business AI practice for mid-market firms, built around fixed-fee discovery and subscription delivery teams. It is another sign that deployment and enablement work is becoming a product in its own right.

items.title: Four in five big companies run AI agents; few can tie the spend to profit
items.summary: Genpact surveyed more than 2,000 executives in 17 industries. Agents are in production at 79% of their companies, but only 15% have fully linked AI investment to profit-and-loss results, and about half of funded projects delivered the value expected.

items.title: Companies talk about AI automation far more than they build it
items.summary: An automation consultancy went through six months of its own client calls. AI came up in roughly half of them, yet only 22% of the organizations asking for AI automation reached a live deployment or an active build. A vendor's own data, so read it as one firm's view.

items.title: Where the AI and creative-tool jobs are this month
items.summary: A count of 6,907 open roles on the careers pages of 151 AI, design and creator-tool companies. Half sit at 26 AI-first companies, about one in five is remote, and San Francisco alone accounts for 37%.

items.title: The week AI agents got an off switch
items.summary: A business-reader digest whose theme is control: CrowdStrike introduced an admin-triggered shutdown for agents that misbehave, and Adobe made its customer-experience agent usable from inside ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot. Useful context for anyone writing AI usage rules.

items.title: Agents are trusted with small jobs, not yet the important ones
items.summary: IT leaders describe handing agents low-risk tasks while keeping a person in the loop for anything business-critical. The piece cites KPMG's summer survey, in which 62% of IT leaders were building or deploying agents, up from 53% a quarter earlier.

items.title: Half of US workers use AI on the job, but daily use is still rare
items.summary: Stanford faculty and students take stock of AI at work a year on. About half of American employees say they use it in their jobs, while only 13% use it every day: the gap between having the tools and changing how work gets done.

items.title: 'AI' now appears in three times as many kinds of job title, mostly outside tech
items.summary: Indeed's Hiring Lab found the number of US professions with AI in the job title has more than tripled since 2022, and that roughly 63% of those titles are in non-tech occupations. This is the trend this board exists to serve.

items.title: McKinsey's 2026 survey: more companies are scaling AI, returns are still catching up
items.summary: The annual State of AI survey reports that 44% of organizations using AI are now scaling it across the business, with agent use growing fastest at large companies, while most are still working to turn spending into measurable results.
